messages:
olivia: heads-up — ACME support pinged about large p99 spikes and intermittent 5xxs since last night. they see 500/504 on /v1/generate and auth latency spikes up to 8s. sample request ids: rq_abc123, rq_def456. this started right after eu1 rollout (cuda16 + driver 535 + gpu-fw 2.4.1)

jordan: looking. is this hosted eu1 only or affecting dedicated pools too? any quick logs?

olivia: hosted eu1. model reported: redwood-open-7b. repro (short): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"...","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> hangs ~6s then 504. client also shows retries with 401s while token refresh waits. billing spike from retries noted.

sam: i can repro on a canary node. baseline p95 stable, p99 is jumping ~x4. looks like KV cache miss plus storage tail. on the node `perf top` shows nvme_io_wait high; `iostat -x 1` shows nvme0n1 %util ~99 and avgqu-sz elevated. nvme qdepth at 1024 in our config.

maria: we pushed driver 535.12 + gpu fw 2.4.1 to eu1 overnight, canaries then batch. rolling back one host now. dmesg on affected hosts shows repeated "nvme: I/O timeout" entries.

devops-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T22:10:00: canary rollout to eu1 completed

jordan: if NVMe timeouts are stalling hostfs writes, GPU tasks waiting on KV cache writes can tail out. mitigation plan (quick): 1) route ACME traffic to a fallback low-latency model variant 2) reduce client retry count to avoid billing amplification 3) roll back driver on affected pools 4) add transient auth token caching to avoid auth DB tail.

olivia: ACME agreed to fallback. i've applied routing rule for customer_id=acme -> model=open-7b-fp16 (lower latency variant). also asked them to reduce retries to 2. noted billing anomalies and opened invoice investigation.

sam: my repro steps: 1) set model=open-7b 2) run 100 concurrent requests seq_len=1024 3) p99 used to be ~1.2s baseline -> now ~4-6s. `iostat -x` shows util 99, logs include `nvme0n1: abort/mq timeout` and repeated io completions delayed.

maria: kernel side may be involved — we also rolled host kernel 6.5.7 with a new io scheduler variation in the same window. possible interaction driver+fw+kernel. quick mitigation attempt: lower queue depth: `echo 256 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` and tune scheduler to noop. i'll test on host-eu1-03.

jordan: prefer controlled rollback rather than reactive sysctl changes. starting rollback of driver on pool-3 nodes (5 hosts) now. also recommend holding CUDA16 rollout.

devops-bot: Rollback job #765 started: nodes host-eu1-03 -> host-eu1-07 are in progress

olivia: thanks — I've told ACME support to expect improvement in ~15m and to pause heavy batch jobs. :thumbsup:

sam: adding short-term auth caching: nginx in front of auth-db will cache token validation results for 10s to reduce auth tail pressure. i'll open a small PR for the config.

maria: after rolling back first two hosts p99 for ACME dropped from 5.9s -> 1.4s, nvme util down to ~60%. still seeing sporadic nvme timeouts; vendor firmware/driver combination suspected.

jordan: next steps: full driver rollback in eu1, hold remaining CUDA16 rollouts, contact vendor about fw 2.4.1 interactions, schedule fw downgrade if confirmed, implement transient routing policy for critical customers to dedicated low-noise pools, and write a postmortem. i'll create an incident ticket and assign owners.

olivia: will update ACME and close the escalation if stable after 1h. thanks team.
